plan.title: Offline fixture: gradient descent on a loss bowl
plan.description: A ball on a bowl-shaped loss surface takes gradient steps downhill. Set the learning rate and the batch size, press Run, and watch the path, the next step and the status word. Keep a path, then run again with another learning rate to compare.
plan.reason: Changing the learning rate and watching the same bowl answer is the clearest way to see why a high rate diverges.
interactions: Set the learning rate and the batch size.
Run, pause or take one step.
Start a new run and keep the old path to compare.
assumptions: The loss is a simple formula, not a real model.
The batch noise is simulated and fixed by the run.
limitations: One bowl with one lowest point; no momentum or other optimizers.
plan.learningGoal: A learning rate that is too high overshoots the lowest point and diverges; a small one converges.

artifact.title: Offline fixture: gradient descent on a loss bowl
artifact.description: OFFLINE FIXTURE, not generated by a model. A smooth blue bowl with eight contour lines, a red ball on its slope, an orange path behind the ball and a dark blue kept path, a purple arrow for the next step and a dark grey arrow for the full-batch step, and a status word.
assumptions: Illustration: the bowl is the formula loss = (1.4 x^2 + 0.5 z^2) / 2, drawn at a height equal to the loss. No real data or model is used.

Each step moves the ball by -rate x (slope + noise). The noise acts along z, is larger for a smaller batch and does not fade near the lowest point, so the ball keeps wandering a little at a fixed rate; with all 256 examples there is none. It is fixed by the run and the step.
Diverged means the ball has left the drawn bowl. It is then drawn at the rim, on the surface, and the Loss readout keeps its true value.
Converged means the slope under the ball has stayed small (under 0.12 along the steep axis, under 0.35 along the other) for three steps in a row: it has settled in a band around the lowest point.

Both arrows are steps drawn at 10.7 times their real length, one scale for both, at most 2 long. Next step is the step this batch gives; Full-batch step is the step all 256 examples would give. An arrow shorter than 0.4 is hidden.
A point of the path outside the bowl is drawn at the rim, on the surface, where the ball is held.
